data.definition: A deployable application managed by SiteFlow with repository binding, framework settings, domains, environment variables, and deployment history.
A queued unit of work that resolves source code, runs a Docker build, validates output, and publishes an artifact.
An immutable deployable output produced by a build and stored with checksum, manifest, provenance, and retention metadata.
A non-production route for a branch, pull request, or commit-specific deployment used for review before release promotion.
A named pointer such as production or staging that routes traffic to one immutable deployment and can move during promotion or rollback.

data.title: General-purpose CI/CD suite
data.rationale: MVP builds are deployment-oriented and project-scoped rather than arbitrary pipelines.

data.title: Serverless runtime in MVP
data.rationale: First release should protect static artifact immutability and routing simplicity.

data.title: Owned global CDN
data.rationale: SiteFlow should integrate with existing CDN providers instead of operating a proprietary network.

data.description: Control-plane model and UI/API surface for projects, settings, domains, secrets references, and deployment policy.
Signed Git webhook intake, event normalization, deduplication, and build job enqueueing.
Framework and package-manager detection plus automatic deployment metadata and version lineage.
Disposable Docker build execution with lifecycle state, logs, limits, cache controls, and failure reporting.
Immutable artifact publishing, indexing, verification, retention, and deletion safeguards.
Nginx routing generation and optional CDN cache operations for production, staging, and previews.
Commit, branch, and pull-request preview deployments with stable URLs and retention controls.
Transactional release channel movement between immutable deployments for promotion and rollback.

data.title: Release pointer plus outbox boundary
data.insight: Promotion and rollback SHOULD commit release-channel pointer, audit record, and routing outbox in one database transaction, while Nginx reload and CDN operations run as idempotent side effects after commit.

data.title: Manifest-before-routable invariant
data.insight: A deployment MUST NOT become routable until its artifact manifest is written, checksum-verified, and linked to the deployment record; this invariant connects worker, artifact, routing, and rollback behavior.

data.title: Preview is P1 but route primitives affect P0
data.conflict: F-007 preview deployments are P1, but F-006 routing SHOULD reserve wildcard/path route primitives during P0 to avoid reworking domain and route-key design later.
data.suggested_resolution: Keep preview UI and provider callbacks out of MVP if needed, but include preview-compatible route-key shape in the routing data model.

data.insight: SiteFlow should make artifact manifests versioned, checksum-verified records stored with bytes and indexed in the database before any deployment becomes routable.
Release channels and previews should point to deployments, not artifacts, so rollback preserves source, build, manifest, audit, and routing context.

positions: Data architecture prioritizes protecting active channels, rollback windows, pins, and active previews from garbage collection.
Product and operations may push for aggressive cleanup to reduce self-hosted storage cost.
data.resolution: Suggested resolution: define reference-aware retention defaults with explicit project budgets, protected references, and auditable operator pins.

data.insight: SiteFlow MVP should be API-first with a minimal operator console for project state, build logs, routing status, promotion, and rollback; broad SaaS dashboard and enterprise tenancy should remain out of MVP.
The production deployment loop must be P0 end to end, while full pull-request preview workflow should remain P1 unless routing primitives and wildcard DNS are already stable.
Cross-role consensus supports source_event -> build_job -> artifact -> deployment -> release_channel or preview_deployment as the canonical lineage and audit model.

positions: System and data roles want preview-compatible route keys reserved early.
Product keeps full PR preview workflow P1 to protect production deployment MVP.
data.resolution: [RESOLVED] Keep F-007 workflow P1, but reserve preview-compatible route identity, retention references, and route bindings in F-006 P0.

positions: Architecture requires durable DB, queue, artifact backend, secret provider, and observability choices.
Product needs a clean reference install before public MVP.
data.resolution: [UNRESOLVED] Select database, queue, artifact backend default, secrets provider, and observability stack before execution planning.
